record.original_question: Define a notion of alternating virtual knot, classify alternating virtual knots and alternating weaves on surfaces without stabilization, and formulate and prove the virtual analogue of the Tait flyping conjecture.

evidence.quote: Virtual Alternating Knots: Define and classify alternating virtual knots. Find an analogue of the Tait flyping conjecture and prove it.
Classify all alternating weaves on surfaces (without stabilization).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A virtual link diagram is a 4-valent plane graph whose vertices are decorated either as classical crossings (with over/under information) or as virtual crossings (drawn as a small circle), considered up to the generalized Reidemeister moves. Equivalently, virtual links may be represented as links in thickened orientable surfaces Σ × [0,1], up to ambient isotopy and stabilization/destabilization of Σ. A diagram on a surface is called alternating if, traveling along each component, classical over- and under-crossings alternate; it is called reduced if it contains no nugatory classical crossing. A flype is a local move on a diagram that rotates a tangle by 180° while moving a single crossing from one side of the tangle to the other.

Carry out the following:

(a) Give a precise definition of an alternating virtual knot (equivalently, an alternating link in a thickened surface considered without stabilization).

(b) Classify alternating virtual knots, and classify all alternating weaves (alternating link diagrams) on closed orientable surfaces, in both cases without allowing stabilization of the surface.

(c) Formulate a virtual analogue of the Tait flyping conjecture: namely, identify the set of local moves (the natural candidate being flypes) such that any two reduced alternating diagrams of the same alternating virtual link, on possibly different surfaces (without stabilization), are related by a finite sequence of these moves. Prove this analogue.
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made. Boden–Karimi and Karimi's PhD thesis develop the theory of alternating virtual knots and prove a Kauffman–Murasugi–Thistlethwaite-type theorem for alternating links in thickened surfaces (minimal crossings, common writhe). A virtual flyping theorem has been announced and posted (arXiv:2210.03720), adapting Menasco–Thistlethwaite's geometric proof to the virtual / thickened-surface setting for alternating virtual links. However, version history of that preprint indicates substantive revisions, and a complete classification of all alternating weaves on surfaces without stabilization is not fully resolved, so the program is partially solved rather than completely settled.

status_evidence.title: The virtual flyping theorem
status_evidence.snippet: Adapts the geometric proof of Tait's flyping conjecture to alternating links in thickened surfaces and to alternating virtual links, using work of Boden–Karimi.
status_evidence.claim: A virtual analogue of the Tait flyping conjecture has been formulated and proved for alternating virtual links.

status_evidence.title: Alternating Virtual Knots (Karimi PhD thesis)
status_evidence.snippet: Defines alternating virtual knots and proves analogues of the Tait conjectures (minimal crossing number, invariance of writhe).
status_evidence.claim: Definition and partial classification of alternating virtual knots have been carried out.

status_evidence.title: The Tait flyping conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Menasco–Thistlethwaite's classical proof of the flyping conjecture, on which the virtual analogue is modeled.
status_evidence.claim: The classical Tait flyping conjecture was proved by Menasco and Thistlethwaite, providing the template extended to the virtual case.
